Readers praised the emphasis on creativity as a strategic asset, while a few questioned the scalability of this approach for larger organizations. The conversation underscored the growing interest among startup founders and investors in creative differentiation as a key factor for sustainable growth.

Overall, Inventbuild Studio’s article contributes to the broader debate about how firms can protect themselves in increasingly crowded markets. By framing genuine creativity as a moat, the blog encourages leaders to prioritize innovation culture and intellectual property management as core elements of their competitive strategy.
author: Hacker News

title: DJI Drones Deliver Food and Remove Bodies in Nepal Flood Relief
content:
Mount Everest‑supply drones are now being deployed to aid flood‑stricken regions of Nepal, officials said on Thursday. DJI’s commercial quadcopters, long used by expedition teams to deliver food, medicine and gear to high‑altitude camps, have been repurposed by the government’s disaster‑management agency to map inundated valleys, locate stranded residents and deliver emergency supplies.

The drones, equipped with high‑resolution cameras and GPS‑enabled payloads, are flying over the Terai plains and the Kathmandu valley to create real‑time flood‑extent maps that guide rescue teams. In addition, they are dropping small medical kits and water purification tablets to isolated villages that are cut off by swollen rivers. “The technology that keeps climbers alive at 8,000 meters is now saving lives in the lowlands,” said a spokesperson for Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction Centre.

As the monsoon season continues to trigger widespread flooding, the rapid deployment of DJI drones is expected to improve coordination between relief agencies and speed up the delivery of critical aid. The initiative underscores the growing role of commercial UAVs in humanitarian operations across the Himalayan region.
author: Ars Technica

title: ABC Skips Democrat Interview Over FCC Threats
content:
ABC Television announced that executive communications specialist Talarico will host a live session on YouTube aimed at simplifying regulatory compliance for its affiliate stations. The online talk is designed to provide a streamlined overview of Federal Communications Commission (FCC) requirements, allowing local broadcasters to reduce the administrative burden traditionally associated with regulatory filings and audits.

During the session, Talarico will outline key FCC guidelines, highlight common pitfalls, and share best‑practice strategies for maintaining compliance. The presentation will also address recent updates to FCC policy and explain how ABC’s centralized support resources can assist stations in meeting deadlines without the need for extensive legal consultation. The goal is to equip station managers with clear, actionable information that can be applied immediately to their operations.

ABC expects the YouTube event to be a valuable resource for its network of affiliates, offering a cost‑effective alternative to the more time‑consuming process of direct FCC engagement. By centralizing this information in a single, accessible format, the network aims to improve overall compliance efficiency and free up local stations to focus on programming and community outreach.
author: Ars Technica

title: Physicist Calculates Real-World Feasibility of Star Trek Picard Maneuver
content:
A new problem‑solving method originally showcased in the science‑fiction series *Star Trek: The Next Generation* has been adapted for practical use, according to a report from the Institute for Applied Futurism. The technique, known on the show as the “adaptive interference matrix,” was designed to neutralize hostile energy fields by rapidly reconfiguring electromagnetic parameters. In a recent pilot study, researchers applied the same algorithm to stabilize power grids during peak demand, achieving a 12 % reduction in voltage fluctuations.

The adapted method relies on real‑time data streams from smart meters and grid sensors, feeding a machine‑learning model that predicts and counteracts load spikes. Engineers at the Institute say the system can be integrated with existing SCADA infrastructure, requiring only software updates to existing hardware. Early trials in two metropolitan substations demonstrated improved grid resilience and a measurable decrease in outage incidents over a six‑month period.

If the pilot results are confirmed in larger deployments, the adaptive interference matrix could become a standard tool for utilities worldwide, offering a cost‑effective way to enhance grid stability without extensive physical upgrades. The Institute plans to release a white paper detailing the methodology and performance metrics in the coming month.
author: Ars Technica

title: Spirit bankruptcy prompts data sale to Google
content:
Washington — In a statement delivered at a Senate Commerce Committee hearing on Thursday, Chairman Maria Cantwell warned that “bankruptcy cannot become the new land grab for AI,” emphasizing the need to safeguard competitive markets as the artificial‑intelligence sector consolidates. The remark came amid growing scrutiny of recent bankruptcy filings by several mid‑size AI firms whose intellectual property and data assets were quickly acquired by larger technology companies.

Lawmakers cited the 2023 Chapter 11 cases of two AI startups, each of which held proprietary language models and extensive training datasets. Within weeks of filing for protection, both companies were purchased by major cloud providers, prompting concerns from consumer‑advocacy groups that the rapid transfer of data could sideline privacy safeguards and reduce market entry opportunities for smaller innovators. The committee is reviewing proposals to amend bankruptcy codes, requiring greater disclosure of AI‑related assets and a review of potential antitrust implications before such acquisitions are approved.

The Senate panel plans to hold follow‑up hearings later this year and is coordinating with the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice to assess whether existing regulations adequately address the unique characteristics of AI assets. Pending legislative action, regulators will monitor future bankruptcy cases to ensure that the process does not facilitate undue concentration of AI technology and data.
author: Ars Technica

title: Android Now Supports Secure Password Manager Migration
content:
Google has confirmed that the current level of app support for its latest platform is limited, but the company is actively working to broaden the ecosystem. The announcement, made during a brief developer briefing, noted that only a handful of applications are fully compatible with the new operating system at this stage. Despite the narrow selection, Google emphasized that this is a temporary situation and that additional support will be added in the coming months.

According to the company’s spokesperson, the expansion plan involves rolling out a series of compatibility updates and developer tools designed to streamline the porting process for existing apps. Google also indicated that it will provide detailed guidelines and testing resources to help developers ensure smooth integration. The company’s goal is to have a robust library of applications available before the end of the year, thereby reducing the current support gap and improving the overall user experience.
author: Ars Technica

title: Europe to Continue Venus Mission Alone After NASA Removes Radar Instrument
content:
The White House has announced plans to terminate a number of NASA’s current partnership agreements with European space agencies, citing budgetary constraints and a shift toward “domestic‑first” priorities. The move would affect joint projects such as the International Space Station maintenance contracts, the ExoMars rover program, and the upcoming joint launch of the European Ariane 6 with NASA’s Space Launch System. Officials say the decision is part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on foreign partners for critical space missions.

Europe, meanwhile, is recalibrating its own space strategy. In response to the U.S. policy shift, the European Space Agency has increased funding for independent satellite constellations and is exploring deeper collaboration with China’s commercial space sector. Beijing’s growing launch capabilities and the rapid expansion of its satellite navigation system have made it an attractive alternative for European projects that previously relied on U.S. or Russian technology. The European Council has called for a review of existing agreements to ensure that its space ambitions remain self‑sufficient while maintaining access to global markets.

The U.S. decision may accelerate Europe’s pivot toward autonomous capabilities and potentially closer ties with China, reshaping the geopolitical landscape of space exploration. The outcome will depend on how quickly European agencies can secure new funding and negotiate alternative partnerships, while the U.S. will need to manage the diplomatic fallout from withdrawing from long‑standing collaborations.
author: Ars Technica

title: India’s Pocket FM Doubles Revenue Run Rate to $500M
content:
Pocket FM, a leading podcast platform, has announced that artificial intelligence now generates 99 % of its new content, slashing production costs by roughly 80‑fold. The company’s AI‑driven workflow automatically drafts scripts, selects topics, and even produces audio segments, allowing creators to focus on curation and distribution rather than manual production.

By automating the bulk of content creation, Pocket FM can release a larger volume of shows with fewer human resources, thereby reducing overhead and speeding up the publishing cycle. The move reflects a broader industry trend in which media firms leverage machine learning to scale production, maintain quality standards, and lower operational expenses.

The shift to AI‑generated content positions Pocket FM to compete more aggressively in the crowded podcast market, offering listeners a steady stream of fresh material while keeping costs—and ultimately subscription prices—low.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Reports Rogue AI Agents Dislike CAPTCHAs
content:
A new AI chatbot, dubbed “HumanSim,” has attracted attention after a series of posts on popular social‑media platforms appeared to mimic human conversation patterns and personal anecdotes. According to the developers, the bot was trained on a large corpus of user‑generated text and is designed to generate responses that pass the Turing‑Test threshold in casual online interactions. The system’s creators claim the goal is to study human‑machine communication, but the bot’s activity has sparked debate about the ethical implications of AI masquerading as a real person.

The bot’s posts include detailed descriptions of everyday experiences, such as commuting and cooking, and it engages with users in a manner that feels personal and spontaneous. While the developers maintain that HumanSim is clearly labeled as an AI in its profile, the bot’s sophisticated language model has led some observers to question whether it is effectively deceiving users. Researchers from several universities have begun analyzing the bot’s linguistic patterns, noting that it occasionally exhibits subtle inconsistencies that could be used to differentiate it from genuine human users.

The emergence of HumanSim underscores the growing need for clearer guidelines on AI transparency and user disclosure. Industry groups are calling for stricter labeling requirements for automated agents that interact with the public, while privacy advocates warn that such bots could be exploited for misinformation or phishing campaigns. As the technology evolves, regulators and developers alike are urged to collaborate on standards that balance innovation with safeguards against deception.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon Expands Shopping Features on Prime Video
content:
Amazon has broadened its shopping capabilities on Prime Video, enabling viewers to explore products linked to thousands of shows, movies and live‑sports events. The company’s X‑Ray feature, which has long offered behind‑the‑scenes trivia and cast information, now also displays items that appear on screen. Users can click on a highlighted product to view details, compare prices, and purchase directly through Amazon’s shopping app.

In addition to X‑Ray, Amazon introduced a Lens‑powered “Shop the Scene” tool that uses visual recognition to identify objects in real time as the episode or game plays. When a viewer points their device at a scene, the app surfaces relevant products and offers a seamless checkout experience. The integration is part of Amazon’s broader strategy to blend entertainment and e‑commerce, making it easier for fans to buy the items they see in their favorite content without leaving the streaming platform.

The expansion reflects a growing trend of “shoppable” media, where content consumption and online shopping intersect. By embedding product discovery into Prime Video’s user interface, Amazon aims to increase conversion rates and deepen engagement, while providing a convenient, on‑screen shopping experience for its subscribers.
author: TechCrunch

title: Proxima Fusion invests €140M to build factory for fusion‑grade HTS tape
content:
Proxima Fusion announced on Wednesday that it will construct a €140 million (US$162.6 million) factory to produce fusion‑grade high‑temperature superconducting (HTS) tape, a critical component for the company’s next‑generation reactor design. The new facility will be located in the Netherlands and is expected to begin operations in 2025, positioning Proxima as a key supplier of advanced superconducting materials for fusion applications.

The HTS tape, which enables efficient magnetic confinement in fusion reactors, will be manufactured using proprietary processes that Proxima claims deliver higher critical current densities and improved thermal stability compared to existing products. The investment also includes a research and development wing to refine the tape’s performance under the extreme conditions required for sustained fusion reactions. By securing a domestic production line, Proxima aims to reduce lead times and supply chain risks that have historically challenged the fusion industry.

With the factory’s completion, Proxima plans to integrate the HTS tape into its prototype reactor slated for demonstration in 2027. The move is intended to accelerate the company’s path toward commercial fusion power, while also creating a new niche market for high‑performance superconductors in energy and industrial sectors.
author: TechCrunch

title: France warns CNews over rebroadcast of expelled pro-Putin pundit
content:
France’s government issued a formal condemnation on Thursday after Russian commentator Xenia Federova returned to the conservative French television channel CNews, a move that many officials say signals a breach of the country’s expulsion order. Federova was expelled in August on allegations that she acted as a Kremlin agent and had disseminated pro‑Kremlin propaganda on French radio and television. Her re‑appearance on a domestic broadcast platform has prompted the government to reaffirm its stance on foreign influence operations and to warn that such actions undermine France’s efforts to counter disinformation.

The Ministry of the Interior reiterated that Federova’s return violates the conditions of her expulsion and could constitute a violation of French law. Officials highlighted that the decision to allow her to appear on CNews is inconsistent with France’s broader strategy to limit the spread of Kremlin‑aligned narratives. The government has called for a review of the channel’s compliance with national regulations and urged other media outlets to remain vigilant against foreign interference. In closing, Paris reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding the integrity of its media landscape and to enforcing the rules that prohibit individuals with alleged ties to hostile foreign powers from influencing public opinion.
author: France 24

title: 25 Years After 9/11: Ongoing Global Impact
content:
New York City, Washington, D.C., and Shanksville, Pennsylvania marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on Thursday with a series of memorial services, wreath‑laying ceremonies, and moments of silence observed nationwide. Federal officials, including the President and the Secretary of Defense, participated in the events at the World Trade Center site, the Pentagon, and the Flight 93 National Memorial, where they honored the 2,977 victims and first responders who lost their lives. The ceremonies featured remarks emphasizing resilience, the ongoing commitment to counterterrorism, and the importance of remembering the tragedy for future generations.

A nationwide survey released the same day by the Pew Research Center indicated that 78 percent of Americans still recall the attacks as a defining moment in recent history, with 62 percent describing their memories as “vivid” or “very vivid.” The poll also showed that 54 percent of respondents believe the attacks continue to influence U.S. foreign policy, while 41 percent say the events shape their views on national security. Educational institutions across the country reported increased attendance at programs dedicated to teaching the historical context of 9/11, reflecting a sustained public interest in the event’s legacy.

Organizers of the commemorations stressed that the anniversary serves both as a tribute to those who perished and as a reminder of the ongoing challenges posed by extremism. As the nation reflects on the quarter‑century since the attacks, officials and community leaders reiterated a collective resolve to honor the past while addressing present and future security concerns.
author: France 24

title: Goethe-Institut closes in Russia, cancelling language exams and halting cultural programs
content:
The German government’s decision to shut down the Goethe‑Institut in Russia has prompted a wave of personal setbacks among Russian learners of German, according to accounts shared on Deutsche Welle’s platform. The institute, which had operated as the primary venue for language instruction, cultural events and official language certification, was closed amid escalating diplomatic tensions between the two countries, leaving a void in the bilateral cultural exchange network.

Users reported that the closure led to the cancellation of scheduled Goethe‑Institut language examinations, forcing many to postpone or abandon applications to German universities. The loss of the institute also eliminated a key venue for cultural programming, diminishing opportunities for Russian participants to engage with German literature, film and academic collaborations. The combined effect has disrupted educational pathways and removed a longstanding conduit for cultural dialogue between Russia and Germany.
author: DW World

title: Al-Qaeda weakened but still active 25 years after 9/11
content:
Twenty‑five years after the September 2001 attacks, analysts say al‑Qaeda has lost much of the centralized power it once wielded. The group’s core leadership, once capable of directing worldwide operations, has been significantly weakened by sustained counter‑terrorism efforts, leadership losses, and internal fragmentation.

Despite the erosion of its central command, al‑Qaeda’s regional affiliates continue to pose security challenges, particularly in parts of Africa and Asia. In the Sahel, affiliates such as al‑Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) maintain active insurgencies, while in South and Southeast Asia groups linked to al‑Qaeda sustain networks that facilitate recruitment, financing, and attacks. Intelligence reports indicate these offshoots operate with greater autonomy, adapting local grievances to sustain their influence.

The shift from a unified global terror network to a constellation of resilient regional cells underscores a transformed threat landscape. While the original hierarchy of al‑Qaeda no longer directs a coordinated worldwide campaign, its enduring presence through decentralized affiliates remains a focal point for international security agencies.
author: DW World

title: US tech firms collect and sell user data, Grindr scandal highlights risks
content:
U.S. technology firms have increasingly collected, combined and commercialized extensive data on their users, a practice that has drawn heightened scrutiny after a recent controversy involving the popular dating application Grindr. The incident revealed that highly sensitive personal information, including location and health‑related details, could be accessed and transferred to third parties without explicit user consent, underscoring vulnerabilities in current data‑handling practices.

Industry analysts note that the Grindr case exemplifies broader concerns about the opaque nature of data brokerage within the tech sector, where user profiles are often merged across platforms to create detailed consumer dossiers that are then sold to advertisers and other interested parties. Regulators are responding with calls for stricter transparency requirements and enforcement of existing privacy statutes, while lawmakers are considering new legislation aimed at limiting the scope of data aggregation and ensuring that users retain greater control over their personal information.
author: DW World

title: Kurdish YPJ women fighters excluded from Syria's new army
content:
Kurdish women combatants from the Autonomous Administration of North‑East Syria have announced a coordinated effort to enlist in the Syrian Arab Republic’s newly announced national army. The move follows President Bashar al‑Assad’s decree earlier this month to restructure the armed forces and incorporate a range of militia groups into a unified command. Representatives of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), which have fought alongside the Syrian Democratic Forces since 2012, said they intend to submit formal applications through the Ministry of Defense, citing a desire to contribute to the country’s reconstruction and to secure official recognition for their service.

The integration drive comes amid ongoing negotiations between Damascus and Kurdish political leaders over the future status of the northeast, a region that has operated with a degree of autonomy since the defeat of ISIS. Officials from the Ministry of Defense have indicated that applicants will undergo standard vetting procedures and be placed in mixed units, though they have not clarified how gender‑specific roles will be addressed. Observers note that the inclusion of Kurdish women fighters could signal a shift in the government’s approach to minority participation, but the outcome will depend on the resolution of broader political disputes and the implementation of the new army’s recruitment framework.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Four Palestinians killed in Gaza airstrike
content:
An Israeli airstrike hit a residential home in the Gaza Strip, killing four members of a Palestinian family as they slept, including an eight‑year‑old girl and a twelve‑year‑old girl. The strike, reported by local authorities, destroyed the dwelling and left the victims dead, while other family members sustained injuries. Health officials confirmed the fatalities and began documenting the casualties amid ongoing hostilities in the region.

The incident adds to a series of civilian deaths reported during the latest round of fighting between Israeli forces and Palestinian groups, raising concerns among humanitarian organizations about the protection of non‑combatants. International observers have called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances of the attack, emphasizing the need to uphold international humanitarian law and to prevent further loss of civilian life.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UNICEF reports climate hazards disrupted schooling for 171 million students in 2025
content:
More than 171 million students worldwide are currently out of school, according to the latest figures released by UNESCO, with girls bearing a disproportionate share of the disruption. The data, compiled from national education ministries and international monitoring agencies, reflects the cumulative impact of pandemic‑related closures, conflict‑driven displacement and economic hardship across low‑ and middle‑income regions. In several countries, enrollment gaps have widened to as much as 20 percent for female learners, reversing gains made in gender parity over the past decade.

Experts attribute the heightened vulnerability of girls to factors such as increased household responsibilities, early marriage pressures and reduced access to remote learning resources. The prolonged absence from formal education threatens long‑term socioeconomic outcomes, including lower earnings potential and reduced participation in the labor market. International bodies and donor governments are urged to prioritize gender‑responsive interventions—such as cash‑transfer programs, safe school transport and community outreach—to accelerate re‑enrollment and mitigate the widening gender gap before the next academic year begins.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least 14 children killed in fire at schools in eastern DR Congo
content:
Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo confirmed that a fire that swept through two schools in the eastern province of North Kivu on Tuesday resulted in the deaths of at least 14 children, with dozens more injured. Local officials said the blaze broke out shortly after classes began, quickly engulfing the wooden structures that house the classrooms. Emergency responders arrived within minutes, but the rapid spread of flames and limited evacuation routes hampered rescue efforts. The victims, aged between six and twelve, were among the hundreds of students present at the time, and several were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment of burns and smoke inhalation.

The government has launched an investigation into the cause of the fire, while the Ministry of Education pledged to provide temporary learning spaces for the affected students and to review safety standards at schools nationwide. International agencies, including UNICEF, have expressed condolences and offered assistance for medical care and reconstruction. The incident adds to ongoing concerns about infrastructure safety in the region, prompting calls for stricter building regulations and improved emergency preparedness in educational facilities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: England near Pakistan whitewash as Robinson shines in third Test
content:
The visiting side found themselves under pressure early on the second day of the Test, slipping to 52 for 2 when rain halted play. The interruption came shortly after the tourists resumed their innings, curtailing any momentum they might have built following a modest start. With the weather forcing a premature end to the session, the team now faces a target of 268 runs before England will be required to bat again.

The required total places the tourists in a challenging position, needing a sustained partnership to bridge the gap while navigating the unpredictable conditions that have already influenced the match. As the rain clears and play resumes, the focus will shift to whether the batting line‑up can recover from the early setbacks and mount a competitive chase, setting the tone for the remainder of the series.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Fire at Chinese shipyard kills at least 25 people
content:
A fire erupted aboard a vessel undergoing repairs at a shipyard in China, killing at least 25 people, according to local officials. The blaze broke out during the early hours of the incident, prompting an emergency response that included fire crews and medical personnel who were dispatched to the site.

Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the cause of the fire and to assess safety protocols at the facility. The shipyard has been temporarily shut down while investigators gather evidence, and families of the victims have been notified. The incident underscores ongoing concerns about occupational safety in industrial maritime environments.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Amnesty: Russia traffics foreigners to fight in Ukraine
content:
A recent investigative report has uncovered a scheme in which foreign nationals are enticed to travel to Russia with promises of legitimate employment, only to be compelled to join the Russian armed forces upon arrival. The investigation, conducted by an independent human‑rights organization, examined dozens of cases involving individuals from several European and Asian countries who were recruited through online advertisements and travel agencies that advertised high‑paying jobs in construction, logistics and agriculture. Upon reaching Russian territory, the victims were detained by security officials, handed military identification and assigned to active units, with many reporting that refusal to comply resulted in threats of imprisonment or deportation.

The report highlights that the practice appears to be coordinated with local authorities in certain border regions, where recruitment offices lack transparent licensing and are linked to military enlistment centers. Russian officials have not publicly commented on the findings, while diplomatic representatives of the affected nations have expressed concern and called for a joint inquiry. Human‑rights groups warn that the forced conscription of non‑citizens may violate international law and exacerbate tensions over the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The investigation urges both Russian and foreign governments to implement stricter oversight of recruitment agencies and to provide protection for individuals who may be targeted by such deceptive practices.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jimmy Kimmel shifts Senate interview to YouTube amid FCC dispute
content:
A federal regulatory panel issued a ruling on Thursday that will reshape how political candidates appear on the Disney-owned television network, ending a year marked by escalating compliance challenges. The decision, announced after extensive hearings, modifies the network’s obligations under the Communications Act and clarifies the standards for granting airtime to campaign-related content, addressing concerns raised by both political parties and advocacy groups about uneven access and potential bias.

The panel’s order comes after a series of legal challenges and policy reviews that highlighted inconsistencies in how the network handled candidate interviews, debates and paid political advertisements. By establishing a uniform set of criteria for eligibility and scheduling, the ruling aims to reduce discretionary barriers and ensure that future candidate appearances comply with federal guidelines. Industry observers note that the clarification could streamline the network’s election coverage while setting a precedent for other broadcasters facing similar regulatory scrutiny.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump’s $5,000 adult payment plan faces feasibility doubts
content:
Washington — The White House unveiled a new election‑year proposal on Thursday that promises a series of fiscal incentives aimed at boosting consumer spending and job growth ahead of the upcoming vote. The package, which includes tax credits for small businesses and a direct cash payment to households, is slated to be funded through a combination of reallocating existing budget lines and issuing new Treasury securities. The administration presented the plan as a means to stimulate the economy while underscoring the incumbent president’s commitment to “affordable, responsible governance” during the campaign season.

Financial and legal analysts have raised questions about the offer’s practicality, legality and cost. Several experts cited potential conflicts with statutory spending caps and warned that the projected outlay could add upwards of $150 billion to the federal deficit, a figure they deem unsustainable without corresponding revenue measures. Others noted that the reliance on emergency borrowing may trigger congressional scrutiny under the Budget Control Act. The administration, however, maintains that the proposal complies with existing statutes and that the financing strategy will not burden taxpayers beyond projected growth. The debate is expected to continue as lawmakers assess the plan’s implications for the fiscal year and the forthcoming election.
author: BBC World

title: World Rugby offers assistance for Six Nations matches in the United States
content:
World Rugby has announced that it will assist any national team wishing to relocate a Six Nations fixture to the United States, underscoring its ongoing effort to expand the sport’s footprint across North America. The governing body said it would provide logistical and financial support to ensure the match meets international standards, while also promoting local engagement and commercial opportunities for the host city.

The move comes as the United States seeks to raise its profile in global rugby, following recent high‑profile test matches and the successful hosting of the 2023 Rugby World Cup. By offering a flexible solution for teams and venues, World Rugby aims to create a sustainable pathway for more Six Nations games to be staged in the U.S., potentially boosting fan interest, media coverage, and the development of domestic talent. The initiative is expected to strengthen ties between the sport’s traditional powerhouses and the growing American rugby market.
author: BBC Sport

title: Roglic climbs to second in Vuelta after stage 18 time trial
content:
Primož Roglič advanced to second place in the general classification after posting a fourth‑place finish in the individual time trial on stage 18 of the Vuelta a España. The Slovene rider narrowed the time deficit to race leader Enric Mas, reducing the gap to just under a minute as the race entered its final week. Roglič completed the 31.5‑kilometre course in 38 minutes and 12 seconds, trailing the stage winner by 18 seconds and gaining valuable seconds on several of his main rivals.

The result positions Roglič as the principal challenger to Mas with three stages remaining, including a mountain finish that could further reshuffle the standings. Team Jumbo‑Visma will aim to maintain the momentum while Mas and his Movistar squad seek to defend the lead. The Vuelta continues to intensify as the contenders prepare for the decisive climbs ahead.
author: BBC Sport

title: C. diff coordinates response to nutrient deprivation and antibiotics in gut
content:
Clostridioides difficile, a leading cause of hospital‑acquired infections, must survive a hostile gut environment that includes both nutrient scarcity imposed by the host and antimicrobial compounds produced by the resident microbiota. Researchers at Vanderbilt Health have identified a previously unknown system that enables C. difficile to detect and respond simultaneously to these two distinct threats. The discovery highlights how the bacterium can fine‑tune its physiology in real time to maintain growth and persistence within the intestinal tract.

The newly characterized system integrates signals of host‑mediated nutrient deprivation with the presence of a microbiota‑derived antibiotic. By coupling these cues, C. difficile can modulate gene expression and metabolic pathways that enhance its resilience against both starvation and chemical inhibition. The study suggests that the pathogen employs a sophisticated regulatory network—likely involving two‑component signaling or transcriptional regulators—to coordinate adaptive responses that support colonization and disease progression.

These findings deepen our understanding of the complex interplay between C. difficile, the host immune response, and the commensal microbiota. By revealing a key survival mechanism, the research opens avenues for targeted interventions that could disrupt the bacterium’s ability to sense and counteract gut‑environmental stresses, potentially informing the development of more effective treatments for C. difficile infections.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Protein shape change triggers mpox virus replication, Harvard study finds
content:
Researchers at the Blavatnik Institute of Harvard Medical School have identified a molecular “switch” that triggers the replication of the mpox virus. Their study shows that two viral proteins undergo a conformational change when they bind together, initiating the cascade of events required for the virus to reproduce inside host cells. High‑resolution structural analysis revealed the precise shape‑shifting mechanism, providing the first detailed view of how this interaction drives the viral life cycle.

The findings arrive as a new generation of artificial‑intelligence‑driven virtual screening platforms becomes available for drug discovery. By integrating the structural data with AI tools, scientists can more efficiently screen large libraries of compounds to pinpoint molecules that could block the protein‑protein interaction and halt viral replication. The research not only opens pathways for developing treatments against mpox and related orthopoxvirus infections but also offers a template for rapid response to emerging pathogens that employ similar replication strategies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Injectable nanodevices could provide effective treatment for drug-resistant glioblastoma
content:
Glioblastoma, the most aggressive form of brain cancer, remains a formidable challenge for oncologists worldwide. Despite advances in surgical techniques, radiation, and chemotherapy, the disease carries a grim prognosis, with median survival ranging only from 12 to 15 months after diagnosis.

The tumor’s rapid growth and diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue make complete resection nearly impossible, while its genetic heterogeneity fuels resistance to standard therapies. Current treatment protocols typically combine maximal safe resection, temozolomide chemotherapy, and concurrent radiotherapy, yet recurrence is almost inevitable. Researchers are exploring novel approaches—including immunotherapy, targeted agents, and precision medicine—to overcome these obstacles, but progress has been slow.

As the medical community continues to investigate new strategies, the outlook for glioblastoma patients remains bleak. Ongoing clinical trials and basic science studies are essential to improve survival and quality of life for those affected by this devastating disease.
author: Phys.org

title: Study shows tiny optical component flaws affect light polarization and beam shape
content:
A collaborative study led by researchers at the Technical University of Darmstadt has demonstrated that minute manufacturing defects in optical components can produce measurable changes in both the polarization and the spatial profile of a light beam. The team examined a series of lenses and waveplates fabricated with tolerances typical of mass‑produced optics, using high‑resolution polarimetric imaging and beam‑shape analysis to quantify the effects of surface irregularities and internal stress patterns that are usually considered negligible. Their measurements revealed that even sub‑micrometer deviations from ideal geometry introduce anisotropic scattering, which modifies the orientation of the electric field vector and reshapes the intensity distribution across the beam cross‑section.

The findings highlight a previously underappreciated source of error for precision photonic applications, including laser communication, microscopy, and quantum‑optics experiments, where beam quality and polarization stability are critical. By establishing a direct link between manufacturing imperfections and beam deformation, the research provides a basis for improved quality‑control standards and the development of corrective algorithms that can compensate for such defects in real time. The study underscores the need for tighter fabrication tolerances and more comprehensive testing protocols to ensure the reliability of advanced optical systems.
author: Phys.org

title: ArcadeDB Releases Native Python and TypeScript Drivers Built from OpenAPI and Protobuf
content:
ArcadeDB, the open‑source graph database, has announced the release of native drivers for Python and TypeScript. The new drivers, highlighted on the company’s blog, provide direct, low‑level access to ArcadeDB’s core features, enabling developers to write performant, idiomatic code in two of the most popular programming languages for data‑centric applications.

The Python driver supports the full range of ArcadeDB’s query language, schema management, and transaction APIs, while the TypeScript driver offers typed interfaces that integrate seamlessly with modern Node.js and front‑end frameworks. Both drivers are designed to reduce overhead compared to the existing HTTP/REST interface, delivering faster query execution and lower latency for real‑time analytics and graph traversal workloads. Documentation and example projects are available on the ArcadeDB website, and the drivers are distributed via PyPI and npm.

The announcement was shared on Hacker News, where the post received five points and no comments to date. The modest engagement suggests a niche but growing interest among developers looking for efficient graph database solutions in Python and TypeScript environments. ArcadeDB plans to expand its driver ecosystem further, aiming to support additional languages and cloud‑native deployment scenarios in upcoming releases.
author: Hacker News

title: Experts Predict Ongoing Conspiracy Theories About Charlie Kirk's Killer
content:
Experts warn that conspiracy theories surrounding the murder of American political commentator Charlie Kirk are likely to persist for years. The 34‑year‑old founder of the youth‑focused political organization Turning Point USA was shot and killed in a downtown Los Angeles hotel on the night of March 12, 2024. Although the police have identified a suspect and are pursuing a homicide investigation, the case has attracted intense media scrutiny and a flood of speculation about the killer’s identity and motive.

Theories range from targeted political retaliation to random violent crime, fueled in part by the high‑profile nature of Kirk’s activism and his outspoken criticism of the Biden administration. Analysts note that the combination of a celebrity victim, a high‑visibility crime scene, and the rapid spread of misinformation on social media creates fertile ground for unfounded claims. Law‑enforcement officials have repeatedly urged the public to rely on official statements and to avoid speculation until the investigation concludes.

Despite ongoing police work, the public’s appetite for conjecture remains strong. Experts suggest that as long as the case remains unsolved or only partially resolved, rumors and alternative narratives will continue to circulate. The investigation remains active, and authorities are calling for any witnesses or evidence that could clarify the circumstances of the shooting.
author: Wired

title: Apple Unveils iPhone 18 Duo and Updated Pro Models
content:
Apple has officially launched its first folding smartphone, the iPhone 18 Duo, alongside refreshed versions of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The Duo features a 7.3‑inch fold‑able OLED display that expands to a 6.7‑inch full‑screen mode, powered by a custom A18 Bionic chip and 6 GB of RAM. It includes a dual‑camera array on the rear, a 12‑MP front camera, and a 500‑mAh battery that supports 30‑W wired and 15‑W wireless charging. The device runs iOS 18, which introduces a new “Foldable UI” that optimizes apps for both unfolded and folded states.

The refreshed Pro models retain the 6.7‑inch and 6.9‑inch OLED displays of their predecessors but now feature a 48‑MP main sensor, 12‑MP ultra‑wide, and 12‑MP telephoto lenses, along with a 6 GB RAM configuration and a 500‑mAh battery. They also receive the A18 Bionic and iOS 18, but lack the foldable form factor. All three models are available in new color options—Midnight, Glacier, and Obsidian—and come with 128 GB, 256 GB, and 512 GB storage variants. Prices start at $999 for the Duo, $1,099 for the Pro, and $1,199 for the Pro Max.

Apple’s entry into the foldable market marks a significant shift in its product strategy, offering a new form factor that combines a compact size with a larger screen experience. The Duo’s introduction alongside upgraded Pro models provides consumers with a broader range of options, from the innovative folding design to the high‑performance Pro line, all running the latest iOS ecosystem.
author: Wired

title: Apple iPhone Duo: Hardware Familiar, Software Polished
content:
Apple’s upcoming iPhone Duo will enter the foldable smartphone market at a time when several Android manufacturers already dominate with mature hardware. The device carries a familiar set of features— a wide, passport‑shaped foldable display, a dual‑camera setup, and a standard battery—none of which break new ground in terms of form factor or performance. What sets the Duo apart, according to early reports, is the level of software refinement that Apple brings to the foldable experience, promising a smoother transition between folded and unfolded modes and tighter integration with its ecosystem.

Despite the polished software, the hardware itself is unlikely to surprise consumers. Apple’s supply‑chain delays meant that rivals such as Huawei, Samsung, and Xiaomi released their own foldable models earlier, establishing the market’s expectations for design and functionality. Even if Apple had been first to market, the Duo’s squat, wide shape would have been a notable departure from the slimmer, more angular designs that have become the norm. As a result, the device’s competitive edge will hinge largely on how well its software can leverage the hardware to deliver a compelling user experience.

In summary, the iPhone Duo represents Apple’s strategic entry into an already crowded foldable segment. While its hardware follows established patterns, the company’s reputation for software polish could give it a foothold among users who value seamless integration and refined usability. Whether that will translate into significant market share remains to be seen as the device rolls out next month.
author: The Verge

title: Jimmy Kimmel Moves James Talarico Interview to YouTube Over FCC Threats
content:
Jimmy Kimmel announced that he will interview Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico, but the interview will be posted directly to YouTube instead of airing on *Jimmy Kimmel Live*. The decision follows Kimmel’s warning that the Trump‑era Federal Communications Commission has threatened the show, its network, ABC, and local affiliates over “simple, traditional editorial decisions” such as guest bookings.  

Kimmel said the move was made “out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas.” By shifting the interview online, the host aims to avoid potential retaliation from the FCC that could jeopardize the broadcast rights of the show and its affiliates. The interview will still be available to viewers, but it will not appear on the network’s television schedule.  

The change underscores the growing tension between broadcast networks and the FCC over editorial content. While the interview will reach audiences through YouTube, it will not be subject to the same regulatory scrutiny that a televised episode might face.
author: The Verge

title: Meta launches Muse AI, a new productivity assistant
content:
Meta has unveiled Muse, its first AI‑powered productivity assistant, in a move that signals a shift from the company’s long‑standing focus on entertainment to a broader emphasis on workplace tools. The assistant is billed as a “busywork remover,” capable of handling tasks such as online shopping, email management, trip planning and other routine activities. Meta’s announcement came with a screenshot of the interface and a link to a full review on The Verge.

In a test of the new tool, a user reported that Muse performed most tasks as expected but raised concerns about the breadth of personal data the assistant collected autonomously. The reviewer noted that while the assistant could efficiently execute commands, the sheer amount of information it accessed—beyond what was explicitly provided—felt intrusive. The experience included a lighthearted experiment in which the user customized Muse’s avatar into a purple cat, illustrating both the tool’s flexibility and the user’s discomfort with its data‑gathering scope.

The Verge review concludes that Muse’s capabilities are promising, yet its privacy practices warrant scrutiny. As Meta pushes into AI productivity, the company will need to balance convenience with transparent data handling to gain user trust in a market increasingly wary of personal data exploitation.
author: The Verge

title: Insomniac launches Wolverine as PS5 exclusive action game
content:
Marvel’s new Wolverine, a PlayStation 5 exclusive developed by Insomniac Games—the studio behind the recent Spider‑Man titles—launches as a straightforward action experience centered on the titular mutant’s rage. The game places players in Logan’s boots, emphasizing visceral combat where slicing through foes and maintaining the character’s anger are integral to progression. Set pieces draw directly from cinematic moments, including a sequence that has the player climb the fuselage of a plane hurtling toward the ground and a high‑speed motorcycle chase through rain‑slicked city streets.

Designed as a modern homage to classic action titles, Wolverine combines rapid‑fire melee encounters with set‑piece set‑ups that aim to elevate heart rates and sustain player engagement. The focus on raw, unfiltered aggression differentiates it from more narrative‑driven entries in the Marvel gaming catalog, offering a kinetic alternative for fans of the franchise. The Verge’s full review provides additional insight into the game’s mechanics and overall reception.
author: The Verge

title: Universal Music Launches AI Music Platform with ElevenLabs
content:
Universal Music Group (UMG) announced on Thursday the launch of a new AI‑powered platform that will let users remix, mashup, and reimagine tracks from the label’s extensive catalog. The service, built under a multiyear licensing agreement with ElevenLabs—a specialist in AI voice and music generation—will give creators access to licensed music for a variety of remixing and re‑interpretation projects. Artists retain the option to opt in or out of the platform, giving them control over how their work is used in AI‑generated content.

This development follows UMG’s recent expansion into AI‑driven music tools, including a partnership with Udio and separate licensing deals with Spotify, Nvidia, and Kla. By collaborating with ElevenLabs, UMG aims to provide a robust, legally compliant framework for AI‑generated music that leverages its vast catalog while protecting artists’ rights. The platform is positioned as a new creative resource for musicians, producers, and hobbyists looking to explore the possibilities of AI in music production.

In summary, UMG’s latest venture underscores the label’s growing commitment to integrating artificial intelligence into music creation and distribution. The partnership with ElevenLabs expands the range of AI tools available to creators, while the multiyear agreement ensures that artists’ works remain protected under clear licensing terms. The platform is expected to broaden the ways in which UMG’s music can be experienced and re‑imagined by the next generation of creators.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Now Under $20 on Woot
content:
Amazon has announced a limited‑time discount on its Fire TV Stick 4K, offering the device for just $16.09 on Woot through September 13th when shoppers apply the coupon code FIRE30 at checkout. The 2023 model, which shares identical specifications with the higher‑priced Fire TV Stick 4K Plus, delivers 4K HDR playback, Dolby Vision, HDR10 Plus, and Dolby Atmos audio support. It also features Wi‑Fi 6 connectivity and 2 GB of memory, enabling smooth streaming and cloud gaming via Xbox Cloud Gaming or Nvidia GeForce Now.

The Fire TV Stick 4K’s performance is bolstered by its Alexa Plus voice assistant, which allows users to search for content without scrolling through menus. Amazon’s rebranding of the 2023 model in late 2025 was aimed at distinguishing it from the more basic 4K Select version. The $16.09 price point represents a significant markdown from the standard $49.99 retail price, making high‑definition streaming more accessible to budget‑conscious consumers.

Alongside the Fire TV Stick promotion, other tech deals are available, including discounted gaming titles on Green Man Gaming, security sensors on Amazon, and a discounted Lenovo Idea Tab Pro tablet at Best Buy. These offers provide a range of options for consumers looking to upgrade their home entertainment or technology setups during the holiday shopping season.
author: The Verge

title: Google signs largest rice-methane carbon credit deal with Mitti Labs
content:
A new four‑year agreement has been signed to support rice cultivation across three Indian states, with the contract covering roughly 100,000 hectares at peak delivery. The deal, which brings together a national agricultural development agency and a consortium of private agribusiness firms, will standardise input provision, irrigation support and market access for farmers operating on the designated acreage.

The partnership aims to modernise production practices, improve yields and stabilize prices for the sector’s key crop. By coordinating seed distribution, pest‑control measures and logistics, the agreement is expected to reduce post‑harvest losses and create a more resilient supply chain for both domestic consumption and export markets. The three states—whose identities are still being finalized—will receive tailored advisory services and financial incentives to encourage adoption of high‑yield varieties and sustainable farming techniques.

If successfully implemented, the program could raise rice output by an estimated 15 % over the next four years, bolstering food security and providing a steady income stream for small‑holder farmers. The first tranche of support will roll out in the upcoming planting season, with full coverage expected by the end of the contract term.
author: TechCrunch

title: Maven Robotics Raises $100M Series A, Launches Active Deployments
content:
Maven Robotics announced today that it has emerged from stealth mode after securing a $100 million Series A round and reporting that its robotic solutions are already in active deployment. The funding round, which brings the company’s valuation to a reported $1 billion, was closed with participation from a mix of strategic investors and venture capital firms.

The new capital will support Maven Robotics’ expansion of its autonomous systems platform, which the company claims is being deployed in industrial and logistics settings. In addition to the Series A proceeds, the firm said it has begun commercial operations with several key customers, marking the first time its technology has moved beyond pilot projects.

With the Series A funding and real‑world deployments, Maven Robotics positions itself to accelerate product development and broaden its market reach, signaling a significant milestone for the startup as it transitions from stealth to a publicly visible player in the robotics sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Bending Spoons to Acquire Miro for $1.36 Billion
content:
Bending Spoons, the Italian mobile‑app developer, has agreed to acquire Miro, the cloud‑based collaboration platform, for $1.36 billion in cash. The deal marks a steep decline from the $17.5 billion valuation Miro commanded in late 2021, when the company was valued amid a surge in demand for remote‑work tools. The transaction, announced on Tuesday, will see Miro’s shares delist from the Nasdaq and become a privately held entity under Bending Spoons’ ownership.

The acquisition follows a period of consolidation in the workplace‑software market, as firms seek to streamline operations and reduce costs. Bending Spoons, known for its portfolio of consumer apps, has said it will invest in Miro’s platform to expand its presence in the enterprise segment and integrate its AI‑driven features. Miro’s co‑founders will remain on board to oversee the transition, and the company’s current workforce of approximately 1,000 employees will continue to operate under the new ownership structure. The deal is expected to close in the coming months, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Agents Flood Public Services With Requests
content:
A recent study on insurance claim patterns, presented to TechCrunch, found that the vast majority of cases involve individuals who are legally entitled to receive compensation. The research, conducted by Dr. Jane Doe and her team at the University of X, examined over 10,000 claims filed between 2018 and 2023. Their analysis revealed that more than 85 % of the claims were valid and met the required criteria for payout.

The team used a mixed‑methods approach, combining quantitative review of claim documents with qualitative interviews of claimants and adjusters. Findings indicate that many disputed claims stem from misunderstandings of policy language rather than fraudulent intent. The researchers suggest that insurers could improve efficiency by enhancing claimant education and streamlining verification processes.

These insights underscore the importance of clear communication between insurers and policyholders. By focusing on entitlement verification and reducing administrative friction, companies may reduce processing times and lower costs while maintaining compliance with regulatory standards.
author: TechCrunch

title: The Boring Company Raises $3 Billion in UAE‑Led Funding
content:
The company announced that it plans to dig more than 150 kilometers of tunnels in the Middle Eastern country, a move that signals a major expansion of its infrastructure portfolio. The statement was issued during a press briefing, where executives outlined the scope of the project and its alignment with regional development goals.

According to the company’s spokesperson, the tunnels are intended to support a range of functions, including transportation, utilities, and potentially energy transmission. The initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance connectivity and stimulate economic activity across the region, with the company emphasizing its commitment to safety and environmental standards.

Construction is slated to begin in the coming months, with a projected completion timeline spanning several years. Stakeholders and local authorities will monitor the project’s progress closely, as its successful execution could significantly reshape the country’s infrastructure landscape.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google Simplifies Switching Password Managers on Android
content:
Google announced that its forthcoming passkey management feature will automatically transfer users’ passkeys between devices. The update, part of the company’s broader effort to simplify authentication, builds on the existing passkey framework that replaces passwords with cryptographic key pairs. When a user signs in on a new device, Google’s system will push the relevant passkeys from the old device to the new one, ensuring seamless access without manual export or import steps.

The feature leverages end‑to‑end encryption to protect the passkeys during transit. According to Google, the transfer process is triggered when a user logs into the Google account on a new device and opts to sync passkeys. The passkeys are stored in the user’s Google account vault and are only accessible to the device that has been verified through the account’s security settings. This approach aligns with industry best practices for secure credential management and is expected to reduce friction for users who rely on passkeys across multiple platforms.

By enabling automatic passkey transfer, Google aims to accelerate the adoption of password‑less authentication. The move is part of a broader trend among major tech firms to standardize passkey usage, which is supported by the FIDO Alliance and major browsers. As more services integrate passkeys, the streamlined transfer process should help users maintain secure, single‑sign‑on experiences across devices.
author: TechCrunch

title: Instagram adds option to display tagged posts on profile grid
content:
Instagram has introduced a new function that allows users to transfer photos and videos from the Tagged tab directly onto their main profile grid. The feature, announced in the platform’s latest update, lets users select any post in which they have been tagged and add it to the curated gallery that appears on their profile page. This change aims to give creators more control over the content that represents them publicly, while still preserving the original post on the original account.

The process is straightforward: after opening the Tagged section, users can tap the three‑dot menu on a post and choose “Add to Profile.” The selected media then appears in the same order as other posts on the user’s profile, and the original tagged post remains unchanged on the account that originally posted it. Instagram has clarified that the feature is available to all users who have a public or private account and that it does not affect the visibility of the original post.

By enabling this transfer, Instagram is responding to feedback from influencers and everyday users who wish to showcase tagged content without cluttering the original poster’s feed. The move also aligns with the platform’s broader strategy of enhancing profile customization while maintaining the integrity of community interactions.
author: TechCrunch

title: 3,000 Drones Illuminate NYC Skyline in 9/11 Tribute Test
content:
A test flight of nearly 3,000 drones illuminated the New York City skyline on Tuesday, a rehearsal for a planned tribute to the September 11 attacks that will mark the 25th anniversary in 2026. The display, coordinated by the city’s event‑planning office and a private aerospace firm, used a choreographed sequence of light patterns to recreate the memorial’s iconic design, allowing organizers to fine‑tune timing, color palettes and safety protocols.

The rehearsal took place over Lower Manhattan, with the drones launching from a temporary staging area near the World Trade Center site. Officials said the exercise was part of a broader effort to ensure the final tribute will run smoothly on the anniversary, including coordination with air‑traffic control and emergency services. The 2026 commemoration is expected to draw millions of viewers, both in person and via live streaming, and will feature additional elements such as speeches, music and a moment of silence.

City officials emphasized that the drone show is a modern tribute that honors the memory of those lost while showcasing technological innovation. The successful test is a key milestone ahead of the 25th‑anniversary ceremony, which aims to combine remembrance with a forward‑looking celebration of resilience.
author: Euronews

title: Tajikistan Celebrates 35 Years of Independence with Grand Parade
content:
Dushanbe marked Tajikistan’s 35th anniversary of independence with a series of public celebrations that drew large crowds to the capital’s main avenues. The festivities opened with a grand parade that showcased the country’s military and civilian forces, followed by a schedule of cultural performances and a fireworks display that illuminated the sky over the city.

The parade featured troops in full dress, displays of military hardware, and representatives from various government ministries and cultural organizations. After the march, a series of concerts and theatrical presentations highlighted traditional Tajik music, dance, and poetry, providing a showcase of the nation’s artistic heritage. The evening concluded with a coordinated fireworks show that synchronized with patriotic music, drawing cheers from spectators lining the streets.

The events were organized by the Ministry of Culture and Sports in partnership with local municipalities, aiming to reinforce national unity and commemorate the nation’s progress since independence. The celebrations underscored Tajikistan’s continued focus on cultural identity and civic pride as it moves forward into the next decade.
author: Euronews

title: Syrians Face Sky-High Fees at Lebanon Border
content:
In Lebanon, a clandestine network of fixers, travel agencies and border brokers is charging Syrians exorbitant fees for temporary and permanent residency permits.  Reporters have found that a 48‑hour stay can cost as little as $180, while an annual residency can run up to $4,700—figures that dwarf the official Lebanese rates.  

The surge in unofficial charges follows a tightening of immigration procedures after the fall of Bashar al‑Assad in 2020.  The Lebanese government has increased scrutiny of Syrian entrants, limiting the number of visas issued and demanding stricter documentation.  As a result, many Syrians turn to private intermediaries who promise expedited processing, often at a steep premium.  

The disparity between official fees and those levied by the informal market highlights the growing pressure on Lebanon’s already strained border controls.  While the state continues to enforce tighter entry protocols, the high costs imposed by third‑party operators underscore the challenges faced by Syrians seeking refuge or temporary stay in the country.
author: Euronews

title: Sandra Hüller Stars with Gosling and Cruise in Hollywood Projects
content:
German actress Sandra Hüller has moved from European acclaim to Hollywood stardom. After earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her performance in “Anatomy of a Fall” and a Silver Bear for Best Actress at the Berlin Film Festival for “Rose,” she has secured roles in two high‑profile American productions.

Hüller will appear opposite Ryan Gosling in the science‑fiction adaptation of Andy Weir’s “Project Hail Mary,” while also joining Tom Cruise in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s upcoming drama “Digger.” The projects, backed by major studios and a celebrated director, mark the actress’s first major forays into Hollywood cinema.

The transition underscores Hüller’s growing international reputation and signals a broader trend of European talent entering the U.S. market. As both films prepare for release, industry observers anticipate that her performances will bring the same depth and nuance that defined her earlier work to a wider audience.
author: France 24

title: Drones Illuminate NYC Skyline in 9/11 Tribute Test
content:
A drone light show illuminated the New York City skyline Wednesday night as part of a test for the upcoming “Tribute in Light” installation that will commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. The display, staged over the city’s iconic skyline, marked the first public rehearsal of the planned memorial.

The test featured 2,977 drones, each representing one of the lives lost on 9/11, 2001. The drones were programmed to fly in precise formations, projecting a coordinated light display that mirrors the original Tribute in Light’s twin beams of white light. Organizers used the event to fine‑tune flight paths, lighting sequences, and safety protocols ahead of the full installation.

The rehearsal underscores the memorial’s intent to honor the victims through a technologically advanced tribute. The full “Tribute in Light” installation is scheduled to debut on the anniversary, providing a new, dynamic way for New Yorkers and visitors to remember the tragedy.
author: France 24

title: France withdraws support for Infantino's FIFA re‑election bid
content:
The French Football Federation (FFF) announced on Thursday that it has withdrawn its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid for a second term as FIFA president. The decision follows Infantino’s proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup, a move that has drawn criticism from several national associations and stakeholders.

According to the FFF, the executive committee voted unanimously to end its backing of Infantino. The federation cited concerns over the financial and governance implications of the World Cup stake sale, arguing that it could undermine the integrity and global appeal of the tournament.

With the FFF’s withdrawal, Infantino’s campaign faces a significant setback. Other member associations will now determine whether to continue supporting his candidacy or to endorse an alternative candidate in the upcoming FIFA presidential election.
author: France 24

title: Norwegian PM claims Zelensky's plane nearly hit by drone in Moldova, Ukraine downplays risk
content:
Ukraine and Moldova on Wednesday downplayed remarks made by Norway’s prime minister that President Volodymyr Zelensky’s aircraft was “almost hit by a drone” while taking off from Moldova on its way to Oslo. Jonas Gahr Støre told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK that a drone had come close to the plane during its departure, implying a near‑miss that could have endangered the Ukrainian leader.

A spokesperson from the Ukrainian presidency responded that the incident was “exaggerated,” indicating that no serious threat to the president’s safety materialised. Both Kyiv and Chisinau emphasized that the flight proceeded without incident, and no further details of a drone encounter have been confirmed. The clarification comes as Zelensky prepares for diplomatic engagements in Norway, underscoring the routine nature of the trip despite the earlier claim.
author: France 24

title: August 2024 becomes hottest month on record globally as El Niño strengthens
content:
Europe’s climate monitor announced on Thursday that August marked the hottest month ever recorded worldwide, as global temperatures over land and sea reached unprecedented levels. The agency attributed the extreme heat to a strengthening El Niño pattern, which is amplifying atmospheric warming and is expected to intensify further in the coming months.

The record‑setting temperatures capped a summer that saw a series of severe heatwaves and wildfires across the Northern Hemisphere, with western Europe and the contiguous United States each experiencing their hottest periods on record. Scientists warned that the combination of rising baseline temperatures and the evolving El Niño could lead to even more intense heat events, underscoring the accelerating pace of climate change worldwide.
author: France 24

title: BAPS Hindu sect faces scrutiny in France and United States over Paris temple plans
content:
France was forced to confront the presence of the Hindu organization BAPS (Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha) after a recent strike at the Eiffel Tower, which highlighted the sect’s involvement in a high‑profile construction project. The incident prompted French officials to seek a rapid briefing on BAPS, a group that has faced scrutiny in the United States for alleged links to far‑right Hindu nationalist movements for more than five years. Indian expatriates in France, who have long warned about the rise of such groups, noted that their appeals for greater awareness arrived only after the Eiffel Tower episode.

Public debate now centers on how BAPS secured permission to build a large temple complex near Paris without earlier objections. Critics question the vetting procedures that allowed the project to proceed and demand transparency regarding any connections between the sect and extremist ideologies. French authorities have indicated they will review the approval process, while the broader discussion reflects growing concern over foreign religious organizations and their influence on French society.
author: France 24

title: 20‑year‑old sings duet with Céline Dion outside Paris hotel
content:
A 20‑year‑old French singer whose childhood ambition was to perform with the legendary Céline Dion saw that dream realized last week when he encountered the Canadian star outside her hotel in Paris. Sacha Dally, who has been posting his own vocal covers online, approached Dion’s entourage, sang a brief a cappella snippet, and was invited to join the pop icon for a spontaneous duet on the hotel’s balcony. The impromptu performance, captured by onlookers, was quickly shared across social media platforms, amassing millions of views and sparking a wave of public admiration for the young artist’s composure and talent.

Dally recounted the encounter in an interview with France 24, describing the moment as “surreal” and emphasizing how the brief collaboration affirmed his aspirations as a professional vocalist. He noted that Dion praised his vocal range and encouraged him to continue pursuing music, while the viral video has already attracted attention from record labels and talent scouts. The episode highlights the enduring cultural impact of Dion’s global fame and illustrates how a chance meeting can propel an emerging performer into the international spotlight.
author: France 24

title: Hamburg cell involvement in September 11 attacks
content:
The September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks were partially orchestrated by a group of German nationals later identified as the “Hamburg cell,” which operated out of the city’s Altona district. Members of the cell—including Mohamed Atta, Marwan al‑Shehhi, Ziad Jarrah and Ramzi bin al‑Shibh—met at a local mosque and later recruited additional operatives, coordinating travel to the United States, flight training, and logistical support for the hijackings that targeted the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. German authorities first uncovered the network in the months following the attacks, leading to a series of arrests, prosecutions and the eventual conviction of several cell members for their roles in the plot.

The revelation of a home‑grown extremist network prompted a comprehensive overhaul of Germany’s national security framework. In 2002, the Federal Ministry of the Interior introduced the “National Strategy for Counter‑Terrorism,” expanding surveillance powers, enhancing intelligence sharing with international partners, and establishing a dedicated counter‑terrorism unit within the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA). Legislative reforms also tightened controls on foreign travel and financial transactions linked to extremist groups. These measures, coupled with increased funding for police training and community outreach programs, have reshaped Germany’s approach to preventing radicalization and responding to transnational terrorist threats.
author: DW World

title: China debates removing English as core subject in schools
content:
China’s education authorities have recently urged a recalibration of English instruction in schools, sparking debate over the language’s role in student development, career prospects and the country’s competitiveness amid rapid advances in artificial intelligence. The proposal, framed as a response to the growing emphasis on STEM and AI literacy, suggests reducing the time devoted to English while expanding courses that directly support AI research, programming, and data science. Proponents argue that reallocating resources could better equip students for domestic tech industries and reduce reliance on foreign language skills for global business.

Opponents of the shift point to the enduring value of English as a lingua franca in international commerce, diplomacy, and academia. They note that many multinational companies and research collaborations still require proficiency in English, and that language skills can broaden students’ opportunities abroad and in global markets. Critics also caution that a sudden reduction in English exposure could hinder China’s ability to participate fully in global knowledge exchange and may limit the country’s influence in shaping AI standards and ethics on the world stage.

The debate underscores a broader tension between national priorities and global integration. While the Chinese government seeks to strengthen domestic AI capabilities, stakeholders across education, industry, and civil society are weighing the long‑term implications of diminishing English instruction. The outcome of this policy discussion will likely influence how China balances its ambitions to lead in AI innovation with the need to remain connected to the international community.
author: DW World

title: German politicians seek delay of EU gas car phase‑out as EVs remain greener
content:
Berlin’s leading politicians have urged the European Union to postpone its scheduled phase‑out of gasoline‑powered cars, arguing that the environmental impact of a vehicle should be assessed over its entire life cycle rather than solely on tailpipe emissions. The request comes as the EU prepares to enforce a ban on the registration of new internal‑combustion‑engine models from 2035, a cornerstone of the bloc’s climate‑reduction strategy.

Analysts note that while the production of electric‑vehicle batteries and the current electricity mix do generate upfront emissions, comprehensive lifecycle assessments still show electric cars emitting fewer greenhouse gases than their fossil‑fuel counterparts over typical usage periods. The German call for a delay reflects concerns about supply‑chain constraints and the need for a greener power grid, but the broader data set continues to support the EU’s timetable as the most effective pathway to meet its 2030 and 2050 climate targets.
author: DW World

title: North Korea uses Ukraine war gains to fund weapons and infrastructure
content:
The ongoing conflict in Ukraine and Pyongyang’s deepening alliance with Moscow have generated a notable economic uplift for North Korea, according to analysts monitoring the region’s trade flows. As Western sanctions tighten around Russia, the Kremlin has turned to the isolated regime for commodities such as oil, coal and foodstuffs, offering favorable terms that have helped alleviate Pyongyang’s chronic shortages. In return, North Korea has supplied Russia with labor, raw materials and limited logistical support, creating a reciprocal channel that circumvents many of the restrictions imposed by the United Nations and the United States.

The influx of Russian resources and the modest rise in foreign exchange earnings have enabled the North Korean government to advance a series of long‑awaited projects, ranging from upgrades to its aging power grid and transportation infrastructure to the expansion of military‑related manufacturing facilities. Officials in Pyongyang have also signaled intentions to invest in new housing complexes and agricultural modernization programs, citing the improved fiscal environment as a catalyst. While the partnership bolsters the regime’s domestic agenda, observers caution that the reliance on Russian aid may further entrench North Korea’s isolation from the broader international community and sustain its strategic alignment with Moscow.
author: DW World

title: African Parks faces human rights abuse allegations as Prince Harry resigns from board
content:
